why: UPST-3: the v6/v7 migration documentation is the SOURCE of most rules this tool enforces - temp-disk categories, OS floors, hibernation, quota families, NVMe readiness. A change here can invalidate an engine rule with nothing in our code moving. Watched as a FOLDER so a NEW page is reported too.
how: DOCS-DRIFT-LEARN-1: each page is read from the site with Accept: text/markdown, and the sha256 of the text AFTER the front matter is pinned here. The accepted text itself is kept in textFolder, at the page's Learn path, so a change is shown as a difference from it. Each folder names the toc.json that lists its pages, so a NEW page is still found. A folder path is the Learn path of the GitHub folder it was watched in: articles/ became azure/ for azure-compute-docs and azure-docs, and docs/ became entra/ for entra-docs. Every page's own front matter (source_path) confirmed its GitHub path on 2026-10-03.
license: The stored text is Microsoft documentation, kept for comparison only. Microsoft publishes it under CC BY 4.0 (azure-compute-docs, azure-docs) and MIT (entra-docs), per each repository's LICENSE file, read 2026-10-03. Each file is named by the Learn page it came from.

notWatched.reason: RHUI certificate issues (RHUI-REFRESH-1, KERNEL-OFFER-EDGES-1). A rule rests on it: kernel-update.sh runs its command for an expired RHUI client certificate, limited to the installed RHUI client packages, and the EUS, SAP and HA clients lock releasever. The page is in the Microsoft troubleshooting set, which no watched folder reads yet; read by hand on 2026-11-14 (page updated 2026-06-11). Watching it is RHUI-PAGE-WATCH-1.

Azure Dedicated Hosts (REBUILD-MOVE-HOST-1). A pointer in the reason for a machine the product refuses by scope (2026-11-11); the rule is only that Azure records a dedicated host or a host group on the machine, and no rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

The size list (SCAN-PARTIAL-SUBS-1). A pointer in the message for a machine whose size list the scan could not read; the rule is only that the read failed, and no rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

Azure Resource Graph (LINUX-VERSION-OVERFLOW-1). A pointer in the message for a machine whose facts the scan could not read; the rule is only that the record of the machine could not be made, and no rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

Marketplace purchase plans (NO-PLAN-SCOPE-1). A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; the rule is only that Azure records a plan on the machine or its OS disk, and no rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

Failover clustering. A pointer in the warning that a machine may be a cluster node (CLUSTER-DETECT-1); the product refuses a cluster node by scope, and no rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.
AKS nodes. A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; no migration rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.
Network virtual appliances. A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; no migration rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.
Confidential VMs. A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; no migration rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

Data disk limits of each size (DISKS-32-1). A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope - more than 32 data disks; the limit of 32 is a scope decision, not read from the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.
SAP systems. A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; no migration rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.
Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts. A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; no migration rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.
Scale set members. A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; no migration rule rests on the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

Azure managed applications (DETECT-PATTERNS-1). A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; the rule reads the resource group's managedBy from Azure, not from the page, so a change to it changes nothing the product does.

SQL Server Always On availability groups (DETECT-PATTERNS-1). A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; the rule reads sqlVirtualMachineGroupResourceId from Azure, so a change to the page changes nothing the product does.
SQL Server on Azure virtual machines (DETECT-PATTERNS-1). A pointer in a warning that lets the machine move; no migration rule rests on the page.
Shared disks (DETECT-PATTERNS-1). A pointer in the message for a machine the product refuses by scope; the rule reads maxShares from Azure, so a change to the page changes nothing the product does.
